answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a glacier as the anchor of the cost.
